title: Best S1 Project — RyMeds
story: RyMeds started as a first semester project. Most people in my class were building to-do apps. I wanted to build something that could actually run in a pharmacy — inventory, billing, stock alerts. It won Best S1 Project, mostly because it focused on solving one real problem instead of showing off every feature I knew. The judges liked that it had proper database transactions and could handle concurrent sales without breaking stock counts.

title: Best S3 Project — ETLab+
story: ETLab+ came from frustration. Our college lab scheduling was done on paper, and submissions were emailed around. I built a multi-role system with row-level security in PostgreSQL — students submit work, instructors grade, admins manage schedules. It won Best S3 Project. The hardest part wasn't the code, it was getting the access control policies right so each role only sees what they should.

title: TinkerHub Scholarship Program
story: Selected for the TinkerHub Scholarship Program through the Useless Projects 2.0 hackathon. TinkerHub is a student-run tech community in Kerala. The six-month program (December 2025 – May 2026) focused on learning, mentorship, project building, and community participation. It represented recognition of the work I was putting into learning and sharing with the community.

title: Wadhwani Foundation — Ignite India
story: Completed the Wadhwani Foundation's entrepreneurship program. Learned about product ideation, business modeling, and market validation. The most useful takeaway wasn't about startups — it was learning to think about who actually uses the software and whether they'd pay for it. That thinking now influences how I scope every project.

title: Beach Hack Season 7
story: Participated in Beach Hack Season 7 — a hackathon where you build under time pressure. The experience taught me more about prioritization than any course. When you only have 24 hours, you learn to cut scope ruthlessly and ship something that works. We didn't win, but the codebase I wrote that night was cleaner than some of my semester projects.

title: IEEE Xplore Research Training
story: Completed research training through IEEE and EBSCO. Learned how to search academic databases properly, evaluate papers, and understand publishing standards. Before this, I'd just Google things. Now I actually read papers when I want to understand how something works under the hood.
